paper.title: Miscalculating Area and Angles of a Needle-like Triangle
paper.venue: lecture notes for introductory numerical analysis classes, University of California, Berkeley (version of 4 September 2014; the text is work in progress, not refereed)
paper.text_read: https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~wkahan/Triangle.pdf (fetched 2026-11-19; formulas of sections 1-3 and Table 1 of section 5 taken from the text)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the formulas in the paper; the paper's 10-significant-decimal arithmetic (an HP-15C) is emulated with 128-bit integers (round to nearest, ties away from zero); arctan is a small series written here
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf --cpu=tier3`; the same source also builds natively (-DHOST) for a bit-for-bit comparison

claims_checked: Table 1, Heron's area column (12 rows): sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) with s = ((a+b)+c)/2 evaluated in 10-digit decimal arithmetic equals every printed value to its printed digits, including the three 'Error' rows and the four '0' rows (the published digits range from 3 to 10 significant)

Table 1, accurate area column (12 rows): Kahan's formula (1/4) sqrt((a+(b+c))(c-(a-b))(c+(a-b))(a+(b-c))) after sorting, with its Error test c-(a-b) < 0, equals every printed value digit for digit (12 of 12 exact, including the two 'Error' rows and the two '0' rows)

Table 1, accurate angle C column (12 rows): Kahan's formula 2 arctan(sqrt(((a-b)+c) mu/((a+(b+c))((a-c)+b)))) with mu = c-(a-b) or b-(a-c), evaluated in 10-digit decimal arithmetic and then arctan in double, is within relative 2e-9 of every printed value (12 of 12), and the two 'Error' rows are flagged

expected_values_source.what: Table 1 of the paper (HP-15C results; the paper says a 12-digit HP-71B confirmed the accurate columns to at least nine significant digits)
expected_values_source.tolerance: decimal columns for the areas: exact at the printed digits (the 2e-9 relative tolerance for the accurate area column was declared as the fall-back and not needed: all 12 rows were exact). The angle column, which needs arctan in double after the decimal part, is within relative 2e-9, declared before the first run. The decimal rounding rule (half away from zero) was chosen before the first run.

observations: the paper's other columns (C'' by arccos and C' by the half-angle formula with s) were not reproduced: they need an arccos/arctan in the same decimal arithmetic
the angle column agrees to the digits shown only because the decimal part of the formula (all of the cancellation) is exact in 10 digits; the arctan itself is evaluated in double
negative_control: built with -DNEG_HERON_PARENS (Kahan's area formula with the parentheses removed, a+b+c, c-a+b, c+a-b, a+b-c), 4 of the 12 accurate-area rows no longer match (rows 3, 4, 11, 12) and the program exits 1
not_checked: Tables 2, 3 and 5 of the paper (angle B, its roundoff uncertainty, the side c), and the paper's error-bound arguments
the paper's claims about other arithmetics (IEEE binary formats, CRAY) and about the HP-15C itself; this only emulates its 10-digit decimal arithmetic for these 12 triangles
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison here is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: a 10-digit decimal arithmetic emulated on ounce-core's integer unit reproduces the paper's Table 1 for Heron's and Kahan's area formulas digit for digit and the accurate angle column to 2e-9. It does not show the paper's formulas are accurate in binary arithmetic or beyond these 12 triangles.
